I wish I had not taken that one as an intimate friend. He had already led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me.” And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter.
verses.why: A warning about the friend who leads you away from what is good.

verses.en: And keep yourself [O Muhammad] patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His countenance. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.
verses.why: Seek company that reminds you of Allah, even if it is a small group.

verses.en: O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return all together, and He will inform you about what you used to do.
verses.why: You are accountable for yourself, not for staying accepted by everyone.

verses.en: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true.

O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. How wretched is the name of disobedience after [one’s] faith. And whoever does not repent – then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
verses.why: Don’t be the one who mocks, either.

hadith.en: A man is upon the religion of his close friend, so let each of you look at whom he befriends.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Choose your circle on purpose.

hadith.en: The example of a good companion and a bad companion is like a seller of musk and a blacksmith’s bellows. The musk seller will either give you some, or you will buy from him, or at least you will find a pleasant fragrance. The blacksmith will either burn your clothes or you will find an unpleasant smell.
hadith.by: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: ^Among the seven whom Allah will shade on the Day when there is no shade but His: “two men who love each other for the sake of Allah, meeting and parting upon that.”
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: A believer to a believer is like a building: each part strengthens the other.
hadith.by: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

steps: Practise one calm “no”: “Not for me, but have fun.” You don’t need a long explanation.
Notice how you feel after being with each friend: lighter, or smaller?
Find or build one small circle around something good: sport, study, a halaqah, volunteering.
Step back gently from people who push you towards harm, without drama or insults.

title: Guilt, Shame & Feeling Unforgivable
tagline: “I did something wrong” versus “I am something wrong”
intro: Guilt says you made a mistake. Shame says you are the mistake. The door of tawbah is open for the first, and Allah answers the second by reminding you of the dignity He gave you.

callout.title: Guilt that helps, and shame that harms
callout.body: Guilt that moves you back to Allah and towards change is healthy. Shame tells you to hide and to believe you are worthless. The Qur’an says the opposite: Allah honoured the children of Adam (17:70) and tells those who have wronged themselves not to despair (39:53). Repentance is between you and Allah, and if you have wronged a person, make it right with them where you can.

start.plain: Come back to Allah, as many times as you need. He is not tired of you.

verses.en: Say, “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.”
And whoever does a wrong or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.

And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves [by transgression], remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins – and who can forgive sins except Allah? – and do not persist in what they have done while they know.
verses.why: The key: remember Allah, ask forgiveness, and do not keep going back on purpose.

verses.en: Except for those who repent and believe and do righteous work, for it is those whose evil deeds Allah will replace with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
verses.why: Not only erased, but replaced with good.

verses.en: They said, “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.”
verses.why: The words of Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ (Adam and Eve) ﷺ. They owned the mistake, and did not hide in shame.

verses.en: Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him].
verses.why: After Ādam ﷺ erred and repented, Allah chose him and guided him. A mistake did not end his story.

verses.en: And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.
verses.why: Your dignity was given by Allah, and your mistakes do not cancel it.

verses.en: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.

hadith.en: Every son of Adam makes mistakes, and the best of those who make mistakes are those who repent.
hadith.by: Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a man who lost his camel, carrying his food and drink, in a barren desert, and then finds it.”
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Allah is joyful when you return.

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah will bring the believer close and place His screen over him and conceal him, and say: ‘Do you recognise this sin? Do you recognise this sin?’ He will say: ‘Yes, my Lord,’ until, when He has made him admit his sins and he sees that he is destroyed, He will say: ‘I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.’”
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Allah conceals. Shame wants everything exposed; His response is to cover and forgive.

hadith.en: Allah stretches out His hand at night to accept the repentance of the one who did wrong during the day, and stretches out His hand during the day to accept the repentance of the one who did wrong during the night, until the sun rises from the west.
hadith.by: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: Fear Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good one and it will wipe it out, and treat people with good character.
hadith.by: Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would remove you and bring a people who would sin, then seek forgiveness from Allah, and He would forgive them.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: This is not a licence to sin; it shows how much Allah loves forgiving those who return.

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said about sayyid al-istighfār: “Whoever says it during the day with firm belief in it and dies that day before evening is of the people of Paradise, and whoever says it at night with firm belief in it and dies before morning is of the people of Paradise.”
hadith.by: Shaddād ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Full text on the Du’as page.

steps: Say astaghfirullāh now. Don’t wait until you “feel ready”.
Add a small good deed straight after: pray two rakʿahs, give a little charity, call someone.
If you wronged a person, make it right: apologise, return what is theirs.
Tell yourself the truth: “I made a mistake. I am not a mistake.”
Where it’s a health matter (compulsive guilt, scrupulosity), speak to a counsellor.

title: Feeling Distant from Allah
tagline: When prayer feels empty and your faith feels low
intro: Imān goes up and down. Even the Companions worried about it, and the Prophet ﷺ answered them with kindness. Feeling distant is a call to come back, not proof that you are lost.

callout.title: Doubts and whispers
callout.body: Troubling thoughts do not mean your faith is gone. When some of the Companions told the Prophet ﷺ about thoughts so serious they couldn’t speak of them, he said it was a sign of clear faith (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 132). Ask your questions of someone knowledgeable and kind; there is no shame in asking.

start.plain: Come closer one small step at a time. Allah says He is near.

verses.en: And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me – indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.
And We have already created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than [his] jugular vein.
“Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.”
verses.why: A du’a that even the firmly rooted in knowledge make.

verses.en: Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth?…
verses.why: The verse invites; it does not scold. Part of verse 57:16.

verses.en: Those who have believed, and whose hearts find peace in the remembrance of Allah. Truly, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find peace.
Say, “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.”

hadith.en: ^Ḥanẓalah said: “We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he reminded us of Paradise and Hell until it was as if we could see them. Then I went home and played with my wife and children and forgot much. So I said: ‘Ḥanẓalah has become a hypocrite!’” He and Abū Bakr went to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you remained as you are with me and in remembrance, the angels would shake hands with you on your beds and on your paths. But, O Ḥanẓalah, there is a time for this and a time for that,” and he repeated it three times.
hadith.by: Ḥanẓalah al-Usayyidī (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Imān fluctuates, and the Prophet ﷺ himself said there is a time for each.

hadith.en: ^Some of the Companions came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “We find in ourselves thoughts so grave that none of us would dare speak about them.” He said: “Do you really find that?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “That is clear faith.”
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if they are small.
hadith.by: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
hadith.why: Two rakʿahs you keep are better than twenty you abandon.

hadith.en: ^Allah says: “I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a better gathering.”
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said: “The hearts of the children of Adam are all between two fingers of the Most Merciful, like one heart; He turns them wherever He wills.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, Turner of hearts, turn our hearts to obedience to You.”
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ asked: “What do you think if there were a river at the door of one of you in which he bathed five times every day; would any dirt remain on him?” They said, “No dirt would remain.” He said: “That is like the five prayers; by them Allah erases sins.”
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

steps: Keep the five prayers even if they feel dry. Showing up is the work.
Read a few verses a day, slowly, with a translation. A little, daily.
Spend time with people who make Allah feel close.
Ask your honest questions to a knowledgeable, patient person.
Go outside and look at the sky or trees for a few minutes with a quiet heart.

title: A Habit You Can’t Seem to Break
tagline: Screens, vaping, porn, gaming, gambling… and the shame that follows
intro: Many people struggle with something they keep returning to and hate themselves for. The Qur’an and Sunnah do not shame you for struggling; they give a way back, again and again.

callout.title: This is also a health issue
callout.body: Some habits become addictions, which are real medical and psychological conditions. Needing a doctor, counsellor or support group is not a lack of faith. Help is part of the way out, and it is fine to tell a trusted adult.

start.plain: You are not beyond help. Fall, stand up, ask Allah, and change what makes you fall.

verses.en: Say, “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.”

And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves [by transgression], remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins – and who can forgive sins except Allah? – and do not persist in what they have done while they know.

And if there comes to you from Satan an evil suggestion, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing. Indeed, those who fear Allah – when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him] and at once they are those who see.
verses.why: At the moment the urge comes, remember Allah, and your sight clears.

verses.en: And Allah wants to lighten for you [your difficulties]; and mankind was created weak.
verses.why: Allah knows how weak you are.

verses.en: …And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed.
verses.why: Part of verse 24:31.

verses.en: And those who strive for Us – We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.

hadith.en: Every son of Adam makes mistakes, and the best of those who make mistakes are those who repent.
hadith.by: Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: Fear Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good one and it will wipe it out, and treat people with good character.
hadith.by: Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: A way to respond to a slip: act, don’t sink.

hadith.en: Whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will make him chaste; whoever seeks to be independent, Allah will make him independent; whoever tries to be patient, Allah will make him patient. No one is given a gift better and more vast than patience.
hadith.by: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Allah helps the one who tries.

hadith.en: O young men! Whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and protects chastity; and whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is a shield for him.
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would remove you and bring a people who would sin, then seek forgiveness from Allah, and He would forgive them.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: There are two blessings that many people lose out on: health and free time.
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him)

steps: Remove the trigger: phone outside the bedroom, block the site or app, delete the contact.
Plan the danger hours (late night, boredom, loneliness) and have something else ready to do then.
Ride the urge: they peak and fall. Move your body, drink water, leave the room.
After a slip, don’t spiral. Repent, do a good deed and carry on, as the hadith above teaches.
Tell someone safe, or see a counsellor or doctor. Habits that you can’t control alone often need support.

title: Body Image & Appearance Worries
tagline: Filters, comparisons and never feeling good enough in the mirror
intro: You live in a world of edited faces. The Qur’an says you were created in the best form, and the Prophet ﷺ taught that Allah looks at something else entirely.

callout.title: If this has become heavy or controlling
callout.body: If thoughts about your body or food feel obsessive, or you are skipping meals, purging or exercising to punish yourself, please talk to a doctor or counsellor. This is a health condition and it deserves proper care, with no shame.

start.plain: You were made with care. The filters aren’t what Allah looks at.

verses.en: We have certainly created man in the best of stature.
Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you? In whatever form He willed has He assembled you.

And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.

O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. How wretched is the name of disobedience after [one’s] faith. And whoever does not repent – then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
verses.why: Mocking looks or nicknames is addressed, and that includes how you speak about yourself.

verses.en: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware.

hadith.en: Allah does not look at your bodies or your appearances, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.”
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Looking after yourself neatly and cleanly is fine, and so is accepting how you were made.

hadith.en: Wealth is not in having many possessions; true wealth is the richness of the soul.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: Look at those who are below you, and do not look at those who are above you; that is more fitting so that you do not belittle the favours of Allah upon you.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr: “…Your body has a right over you…”
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Your body has rights: food, rest, care.

steps: Curate your feed: unfollow accounts that make you feel worse about your body.
Thank Allah for one thing your body does for you each day, not how it looks.
Speak to yourself as you would to a younger sibling.
Eat regular meals and move in ways you enjoy, without punishment.
If you feel stuck, talk to a doctor or counsellor, not a trend.

title: Hopelessness: “What’s the Point?”
tagline: When you can’t see a way forward and nothing feels like it will change
intro: Hopelessness is one of the heaviest feelings there is, and the Qur’an speaks to it directly. Even prophets said, “When will Allah’s help come?” and the answer was: it is near.

callout.title: Hopelessness is a symptom, not a verdict
callout.body: Feeling that nothing will ever improve is a common sign of depression, and it lies. It can make the future look closed when it isn’t. Please speak to a doctor or counsellor, and to someone you trust. The Prophet ﷺ taught that every disease has a cure (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5678).

start.plain: This feeling is real, and it is not the whole truth. Allah is near, and relief is closer than it looks.

verses.en: O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and do not despair of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.
verses.why: Said by Yaʿqūb ﷺ after years of grief, when everything looked finished. Joseph’s story was not over.

verses.en: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were touched by poverty and hardship and were shaken until [even their] messenger and those who believed with him said, “When is the help of Allah?” Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.
verses.why: Even a messenger and believers cried out, “When is the help of Allah?” The answer was: it is near.

verses.en: He said, “And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except for those astray?”
verses.why: Ibrāhīm ﷺ said this when told he would have a child in old age.

verses.en: Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life]. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied.
For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.

And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me – indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

hadith.en: ^Allah says: “I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a better gathering.”
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Think well of Allah, even if it is the only thing you can do today.

hadith.en: Your Lord is Ever-Living and Generous. He is shy to turn away empty the hands of His servant when he raises them to Him.
hadith.by: Salmān al-Fārisī (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Raise your hands, even with no words ready.

hadith.en: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not give up.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: “Do not give up” is part of the instruction, not just advice.

hadith.en: Allah has not sent down a disease except that He has also sent down its cure.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Treatment, therapy and support are part of the cure.

hadith.en: None of you should wish for death because of a harm that has befallen him. If he must, let him say: ‘O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is good for me, and take me when death is better for me.’
hadith.by: Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: If this thought is with you, please read the help box below and talk to someone today.

hadith.en: How wonderful is the affair of the believer! All of his affairs are good for him… If something harmful happens to him, he is patient, and that is good for him.
hadith.by: Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān (may Allah be pleased with him)

steps: Do one tiny thing today: a shower, a glass of water, a short walk. Hope often returns after small actions.
Tell one person the truth in a sentence: “I feel hopeless.” You don’t have to explain it.
Don’t decide anything big while you feel this way. The feeling distorts how the future looks.
See a doctor or counsellor. This is treatable, and asking is not a lack of faith.
Read the accounts of Yaʿqūb and Yūsuf ﷺ (surah 12). A man who lost hope for years was reunited with his son.

title: Identity Crisis: “Who Am I?”
tagline: Pulled between family, culture, faith, friends and the internet
intro: Many young people feel like different people in different rooms. The Qur’an gives a steady answer to “who am I?”: a created, honoured human being, with a purpose, accountable to the One who made you.

callout.title: Questions are not a crisis of faith
callout.body: Wondering who you are, what you believe and where you belong is a normal part of growing up. Ask your questions of someone knowledgeable, kind and patient. If this feeling comes with deep distress, see the pages on depression and hopelessness.

start.plain: You are not an accident or a role you perform. Allah honoured you and made you for something.

verses.en: And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.
verses.why: Your starting point is honour, before any achievement or label.

verses.en: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.
verses.why: A purpose, as the Qur’an states it. Worship here includes living with awareness of Allah in everything you do, so a life of study, work and kindness can all be part of it.

verses.en: And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels, “Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.” They said, “Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?” He said, “Indeed, I know that which you do not know.”
verses.why: Humans were given a role of stewardship on the earth, by Allah’s knowledge and choice.

verses.en: And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it, and inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness, he has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who instills it [with corruption].
verses.why: You were given a conscience. Becoming the person you’re meant to be is a matter of caring for your soul.

verses.en: Say, “Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
verses.why: A one-line answer to “what is my life for?”

verses.en: And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteousness and says, “Indeed, I am of the Muslims.”
verses.why: You are allowed to say who you are, with confidence.

verses.en: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware.
verses.why: Your tribe, language and background are part of Allah’s design, not obstacles to belonging.

hadith.en: Allah does not look at your bodies or your appearances, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Identity in Allah’s eyes is what is in your heart and what you do.

hadith.en: Be in this world as though you were a stranger or a wayfarer.
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: A reminder that no place, trend or crowd is your final home.

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said: “Every child is born upon the fiṭrah…”
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Beneath all the layers, the natural inclination is towards the truth. Part of the hadith.

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said to the young Ibn ʿAbbās: “Young man, I will teach you some words: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you; be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. If you ask, ask Allah; and if you seek help, seek help from Allah…”
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Advice given to a teenager about who to turn to.

steps: Write your three most important values (for example honesty, kindness, learning). Check one decision this week against them.
List the roles you hold (child, student, friend, believer). Notice which ones you’re neglecting and which you’re hiding.
Find one person you respect who is both thoughtful and kind, and ask them how they found their way.
Be the same person in every room, even if you’re quieter in some.
Pray, even briefly. It reminds you daily who you’re answerable to and who you belong to.

title: Lack of Purpose & Shared Values
tagline: When life feels aimless and nobody around you seems to care about the same things
intro: Humans feel purpose most strongly when they are part of something shared. The Qur’an describes a community of people who help one another do good, and the Prophet ﷺ gave concrete ways to find a mission worth living for.

start.plain: Purpose is built with others: a mission worth giving your days to, and people who share it.

verses.en: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.
verses.why: The foundation of purpose in the Qur’an. A life lived with awareness of Allah gives meaning to ordinary things.

verses.en: The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakāh and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
verses.why: A picture of shared values: people who help each other do good.

verses.en: By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise each other to truth and advise each other to patience.
verses.why: Even the saving formula includes “advise each other”. It is shared, not solo.

verses.en: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favour of Allah upon you – when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favour, brothers. And you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be guided.
…And cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
verses.why: Partnership in good is commanded. Part of verse 5:2.

verses.en: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do.

And keep yourself [O Muhammad] patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His countenance. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.
verses.why: Find people who call upon their Lord and stay with them.

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said: “No people gather in one of the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it among themselves, except that tranquillity (sakīnah) descends upon them, mercy covers them, the angels surround them, and Allah mentions them to those who are with Him.”
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: Where this site gets its name. Shared study brings sakīnah.

hadith.en: A believer to a believer is like a building: each part strengthens the other.
hadith.by: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: ^The Prophet ﷺ said: “The religion is naṣīḥah (sincere care and advice).” We said: “For whom?” He said: “For Allah, His Book, His Messenger, and for the leaders of the Muslims and their common people.”
hadith.by: Tamīm ad-Dārī (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: A purpose in one word: sincere care.

hadith.en: When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which people benefit, or a righteous child who prays for him.
hadith.by: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hadith.why: A way to think about legacy: what can continue after you?

hadith.en: The example of a good companion and a bad companion is like a seller of musk and a blacksmith’s bellows. The musk seller will either give you some, or you will buy from him, or at least you will find a pleasant fragrance. The blacksmith will either burn your clothes or you will find an unpleasant smell.
hadith.by: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him)

hadith.en: Be in this world as though you were a stranger or a wayfarer.
hadith.by: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him)

steps: Write the three things you want your life to be about, in a sentence each. Share it with one friend.
Join a group that shares those values: a masjid study circle, a volunteering team, a sports or learning group.
Start something small with others: a weekly study circle, a clean-up, a charity drive.
If nobody around you shares your values, be patient. Build a small circle slowly, and keep a few good friends online and offline.
Pick one skill you can put in service of others and practise it weekly.
